$meta.name: Blueprint portfolio design tokens
$meta.description: Single source of truth. Edit THIS file, never dist/. Run `npm run build` (or `node scripts/build.mjs`) to regenerate dist/tokens.css (consumed by the site) and dist/tokens.flat.json (consumed by AI agents and the Figma push procedure).
$meta.architecture: Two tiers: raw palettes (stone = warm content field, slate = cold chrome, ink = primary) and a semantic layer that aliases them via var() references. Components may ONLY use semantic tokens; raw ramp values never appear outside this file.
$meta.themes: A token may carry a `dark` value beside its light one: { "value": <light>, "dark": <dark> }. Only the semantic tier does — the raw ramps are theme-independent, and dark mode re-aliases them rather than restating colours. The build emits those overrides twice: under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` for visitors who never touch the control, and under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` for those who pin it. Components stay theme-agnostic: if a component needs a conditional colour, the condition belongs in a token here, never in a media query in components.css.
$meta.print: A token may also carry a `print` value, emitted last as `@media print` so it beats both screen themes. Paper is a third theme with physical constraints rather than preferences: no backlight, ink costs money, and greyscale is likely — so surfaces collapse to one, the accent returns to ink, and shadows and the skeleton grid disappear entirely. Print values alias the raw ramps like any other token; nothing here is a new literal. Print is not only a colour tier: the `text` scale and `space-nav` carry print values too, because paper needs a different type size (pt, not rem) and has no viewport for a `vw` clamp to scale against.
$meta.size: Type and rhythm are tokens on exactly the same terms as colour: `scripts/check-css.mjs` fails the build on any literal `font-size` in components.css or a page stylesheet. Before this file grew a `text` category the site carried 89 font-size declarations at 40 distinct values, fourteen of them inside a single 0.34rem band — differences no reader can perceive and no system justifies.

color-stone.$doc: Raw: Tailwind stone (warm) — the paper and the prose

color-slate.$doc: Raw: Tailwind slate (cold) — the machine's furniture

color-ink.$doc: Raw: ink (iron-gall, warm-black with a cold undertone)

scheme.$doc: Tells the browser which built-in palette to use for scrollbars, form controls and the canvas. Applied once, in components.css, as `color-scheme: var(--color-scheme)`.

surface.$doc: Semantic surfaces (warm — the paper). Dark mode does not tint the paper blue: it walks the same stone ramp to the far end, so the sheet stays warm and the chrome stays cold in both themes. On paper every surface collapses to one: printers do not render a page background, and tinted blocks only cost ink.

primary.$doc: The ONE changeable brand colour. Everything that reads as 'brand' (headline type, interactive states, the automata's resident ink) routes through these three. Retheme by editing them alone. In dark mode the ink inverts to paper: primary is what the page is NOT, which is why the same components read correctly with no per-component overrides.

content.$doc: Semantic content colours. content-muted is stone-600, not -500: -500 measures 4.4:1 on the page background, just under the WCAG AA text minimum (4.5:1); -600 clears it (6.99:1). Dark mirrors the pairing — stone-400 on stone-900 measures 6.93:1, the same relationship read from the other end of the ramp.

chrome.$doc: Semantic chrome (cold). chrome-label is slate-600, not -500, for the same AA-contrast reason.

chrome-label-on-strong.description: Text sitting on chrome-bg-strong (the footer). Has no dark variant on purpose: that surface is near-black in BOTH themes, so its label must stay light in both. 6.96:1 on slate-900, 7.87:1 on slate-950. It DOES need a print value: on paper that surface turns white, so a light label would vanish.

chrome-grid.description: The skeleton's graph paper — slate-500 at 16% on paper, slate-400 at 14% on dark (a lighter ink at lower alpha, so the grid stays a whisper rather than becoming a cage). It used to be drawn one inset box-shadow per square and is now one repeating gradient per region, which also makes it the whole of what a reader with JS off sees. Prints as nothing: the grid is screen scaffolding, not content, and that is why hiding the automata on paper needs no colour rule in any stylesheet.

action.$doc: Interactive states — always the primary ink. `action` itself was deleted: it aliased `primary` verbatim, nothing consumed it, and a semantic tier earns its keep by being consumed. `action-hover` stays because `.btn--solid:hover` reads it and the distinction (hover is a state, not the brand) is real.

accent.$doc: Blueprint blue, used scarcely. Six places wear it: role underline, section numbers, availability, the automata's hovered cell + user-seeded life, focus rings, and the bar's one primary action. The sixth is the newest and the largest — the Ask / Print segment is a solid accent block rather than the ink it used to be, because at that size ink read as a hole punched in the bar. It is the only place the accent is a GROUND rather than a mark, which is why it is worth naming separately: a second solid accent block anywhere would stop this one meaning 'the thing to press'. The fourth of those moved from CSS into the engine when the cells stopped being elements — a canvas has no per-cell hit area, so the hover tint is drawn rather than declared, and the place it is used is unchanged. The dark value is the same hue lifted to 68% lightness — 47% blue on a stone-900 ground measures 2.42:1, well under AA; 68% measures 5.21:1 on the page and 5.32:1 on the chrome, so the accent keeps its AA rating in both themes without changing hue.

accent.description: Prints as ink, not blue. A CV is as likely to be printed greyscale as in colour, and blue reduced to mid-grey reads as a mistake rather than an accent.

accent-rgb.description: rgb triplet of --accent, for rgba() composition at runtime. It has no CSS consumer any more: its one stylesheet use was the automata square's :hover tint, and squares are pixels on a canvas now — js/automata.js reads this and draws the hover cell and the seeded lineage itself.

effect.$doc: Composited colours that are neither surface nor content — they sit BETWEEN layers, so they cannot be aliased to a ramp step and are written literally here (the one file where that is allowed).

shadow-drop.description: The hard offset shadow under the floating nav — an object lying on the sheet. Deeper and more opaque in dark, where a 15% veil would vanish. Nothing on paper: a shadow printed is just a grey smear.

scrim.description: The veil behind the case-study dialog. Warm stone in light (it dims paper), cold slate in dark (it dims chrome).

automata.$doc: The Squares engine (site js/automata.js) reads these at runtime via getComputedStyle and recomposes them into rgba() — which is why they are rgb triplets, not colours. That held when each cell was a div with a background-color and it holds harder now the cells are drawn on a canvas: alpha varies per cell (an age ramp times the region's breath), and canvas globalAlpha is per-draw-call state, so a triplet is what lets the engine build one fillStyle per alpha bucket instead of one per cell. Living cells are deliberately NOT primary: the resident population is a mid-ramp grey that recedes, so the automata never competes with type.

automata-cell-rgb.description: The resident population — stone-500 on paper, stone-400 on dark (the ramp inverts with the surface, or the cells would sink into the page)

font.$doc: The humanist-machine family: Archivo for display, IBM Plex for body and mono

text.$doc: The type scale: one ramp of thirteen steps, and the line through it is NOT 'above or below body'. It is: is this line's size set by the LEVEL it occupies in the hierarchy, or by the WIDTH OF THE BOX it has to fill? Ten are set by their level, and a level is a decision, so those are chosen rem values — the five chrome steps up to body sit on a fixed ~1.085 ratio, and the five above it (lead, sub, heading, title, display) carry a second chosen value at the grid break. Three are set by their box and stay `clamp(min, vw, max)`: the two posters, whose size IS their container's width, and the statement, a paragraph whose line count would jump six-to-ten on a single pixel of resize if it stepped. Every step also carries a `print` value in pt: paper is a third theme for type exactly as it is for colour, and a `vw` clamp has nothing to scale against on a page. The two `em` entries at the end are ratios, not steps — they mean 'a fraction of whatever set me', which is a relationship the scale cannot express. WHAT THIS REPLACED, because the failure is instructive: the seven upper steps were all clamps, and not one of their numbers was chosen. Four were arithmetic means of the ramps they consolidated and three were verbatim copies, so the tier carrying the most confident prose was the tier with no author. Their `vw` term was also inert at both viewports the doc argued from, and none of their fourteen pin points was one of the thirteen breakpoints the CSS actually uses.

text-2xs.description: The floor. Chips, the tool trace, the source list's ordinals, the ▪ bullets — text you are not meant to read so much as recognise.

text-xs.description: The standard chrome label: the nav bar, buttons, section numbers, dated spans, page notes. Twelve of the old 89 declarations were already this value — it was the de-facto step, now it is the actual one.

text-sm.description: Small prose — captions, fact labels, citation lines, code blocks.

text-md.description: Secondary prose: card copy, list items, definition bodies. Body's quieter sibling.

text-base.description: Body. Set on `body` in components.css; everything else is measured from here.

text-lead.description: The reading lede — one step above body, the paragraph that introduces a section. On paper it collapses back into body: a CV has no room for an emphasised opening size.

text-sub.description: Sub-titles: card titles, a role in an entry, an <h3> inside a case study. Three near-identical ramps used to live here — clamp(1.15rem,1.7vw,1.45rem), clamp(1.1rem,1.9vw,1.45rem) and clamp(1.2rem,2.2vw,1.55rem) — rendering at 1280px as 21.76 / 23.2 / 24.8px. That is drift, not hierarchy. A fourth, the work index's project name, was a genuine step larger and became `text-heading`.

text-heading.description: One step above a sub-title and below a section title: the work index's project names, which are the largest thing in a scannable list and must not fall back to card-title size.

text-title.description: Section titles. At the base value it fits BACKGROUND — the longest of them — inside the well at 320px, which the old clamp's 1.65rem floor did not. It no longer shares a step with the statement: see `text-statement`.

text-statement.description: The one statement per section. It used to share `text-title`, on the argument that the two are the same LEVEL wearing different weights — but they differ by SHAPE OF RESPONSE, which is the distinction that matters here. A title is a single line in a strip that has to land on the lattice, so it steps at the grid break and the step is free. A statement is a 7-19 line paragraph in a measure, so stepping it takes it from six lines to ten in one pixel of resize. It gets an authored curve instead: anchored 320 -> 1440 so both ends are widths the layout actually has, unlike the ramps this scale replaced.

text-display.description: Display: dialog titles, the CV name, a stat, a fact's number. `.fact__num` was clamp(2.2rem, 4.5vw, 3.5rem) and `.stat` was clamp(2.2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem) — a 0.5vw difference nobody chose.

text-display-xl.description: The contact headline. Genuinely fluid, because its size IS its container's width rather than its level. Re-anchored 320 -> 1440.

text-display-hero.description: The hero name, once per site. Genuinely fluid for the same reason as `text-display-xl`, and re-anchored 320 -> 1440. The old floor of 3rem overflowed its own well at 320px — measured, HRISTOV needs 233.5px against 224px of content column — and the old ceiling landed at 1461px, past 1440 where the sheet stops growing and the well starts SHRINKING while the font keeps growing. 2.5rem measures 194.6px, which fits with 29.4px to spare.

text-code.description: Inline <code> inside prose. A RATIO, not a step: monospace runs optically larger than the sans beside it, so it is set relative to whatever paragraph it lands in.

text-unit.description: The unit suffix riding on a display number (`+`, `%`, `×`). A ratio for the same reason: it must stay proportional to the number it annotates, whatever size that number lands at.

weight.$doc: The weight tier. Six steps, all six consumed, and until R4 every one of them was a bare number typed into a rule — 33 declarations at six values, which is the same shape the type scale had before it was tokenised. A weight is a LEVEL, not a decoration: display type is black, a section title is extrabold, a chrome label is medium, and body prose never sets one at all. `scripts/check-css.mjs` now refuses a literal `font-weight` here and in the page stylesheets, exactly as it already refuses a literal size, so the six steps are the whole vocabulary. Names follow the CSS common-weight names rather than the numbers, because 500 and 600 are indistinguishable as numerals in a diff and `medium` and `semibold` are not.

tracking.$doc: Letter-spacing, in two families that do opposite jobs. The TIGHT family is display type pulled together — the larger the line, the more it needs, so the ramp runs -0.01em at a section title to -0.02em at the hero, in steps of half a hundredth. The WIDE family is mono chrome opened up, and it is a plain 0.02em ramp: 0.04 / 0.06 / 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.12. THE UNIFICATION THAT MADE IT A RAMP: the file carried 28 letter-spacing declarations at nine values, and one of the nine — 0.05em, on four selectors including the button — was the only positive value off that ramp. Folding it into 0.06em is the one deliberate appearance change of this phase, and it is what turns a list of nine numbers into two families with a step. `tracking-wide-xl` has a single consumer today and is a candidate for folding into its neighbours; that is an appearance decision and is on the owner's review list rather than taken here.

width.$doc: The display family's variable width axis, named. Archivo carries a `wdth` axis and the file set it thirteen times at six values between 100 and 115 with nothing saying why — six settings inside fifteen units, which is a fifth the width of the axis and the same unchosen band the type scale was consolidated out of. The system is that width narrows as the type comes down the hierarchy: the hero is widest, a section title less so, a statement narrower again, and inline emphasis returns to the natural instance. These carry the whole declaration value, axis tag included, for the same reason `rule` does — a token here is what a component writes, not a fragment it has to assemble. Their DTCG `$type` is `other`: an axis tag plus a number is a value a design-token type system has no name for. `width-display` and `width-normal` have one consumer each and are candidates for folding; that is on the owner's review list.

space.$doc: Rhythm, in two halves that answer different questions. `space-1..7` is a fixed 4px-based ramp (4/8/12/16/20/24/32) for space INSIDE a component — a chip's padding does not want to know how tall the window is. The fluid tokens are for space BETWEEN things, where the page's own rhythm should breathe with the viewport: `pad`/`pad-y` are the content well's inset, `space-flow*` are the vertical steps between blocks, and `space-nav` is the one clearance every page head needs under the floating bar. `space-nav` is the only spacing token with a `print` value, and it is 0 — the bar it clears does not exist on paper, and the same three page stylesheets each used to reset it by hand.

space-nav.description: Clearance under the fixed nav bar, on every page head. Prints as nothing: `.bar` is display:none on paper, so the clearance would be 88px of blank at the top of the sheet.

pad-y.description: The vertical inset of every content well, and therefore the page's section rhythm. TWO LATTICE CELLS, not a viewport clamp: it was clamp(2rem, 5vh, 3.5rem), which resolved to 36px in a 720px-tall window — 1.5 cells, off the grid the terminator exists to keep every plate on, and a different fraction of a cell at every window height. Horizontal inset stays fluid (`pad`) because a measure should breathe with the viewport; vertical rhythm is structure, and structure is measured in cells here. Expressed against `space-6` rather than as 3rem so the two cannot drift apart — change the lattice and the section rhythm follows it, exactly as the strip's height and the rail's width already do.

border.$doc: Rule shorthands. Used as border/box-shadow values in chrome; the square skeleton itself never uses border (inset shadows keep fr-track math exact).

rule-strong.description: The heavy rule. In light it is drawn ink — the section signature. Inverting it literally would make it a 2px stone-50 bar glaring across every section top, so on dark it becomes the strong chrome border instead: still structural, no longer a light source. On paper it returns to ink — the one place the rule is cheap and does the most work.
